skill.name: routeros-app-yaml
skill.description: Create and review RouterOS /app YAML for MikroTik container applications. Use it for tikapp files, app store entries, port mappings, configs, volumes, networks, and validation guidance.
skill.summary: Create and validate RouterOS /app YAML for MikroTik container applications.
skill.author: tikoci

security_audit.summary: Static findings were almost all false positives caused by Markdown inline code, fenced examples, RouterOS placeholder URLs, schema URLs, and illustrative REST snippets. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or host-side command execution was found. The remaining issue is weak example credentials in RouterOS app examples, which should be replaced with placeholders.

remediation.suggestion: Replace admin:admin, changeme, and admin passwords with placeholders that require unique generated secrets.

remediation.issue: Examples use floating container tags and auto-update behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend pinned image versions and explain the update review process for production RouterOS apps.

static_findings.snippet: RouterOS 7.21 introduced the `/app` path (built-in app listing and management). The full YAML app cr
The `/app` subsystem lets users define one or more containers as a single "application" in YAML. Rou
- Each `/app` is defined by a YAML document with services, configs, volumes, and networks
- The YAML is loaded into RouterOS via CLI (`/app/add yaml-url=...`) or REST API
- Built-in apps ship with RouterOS (visible at `GET /rest/app`)
| Environment | `KEY=value` or list | Same, but placeholders expand |
| Configs | Docker configs API | Inline `content` only |
| `name` | string | No | Unique identifier for the /app |
| `descr` | string | No | Human-readable description shown in app UI |
| `icon` | string (URI) | No | Icon URL (shown in WebFig with `show-in-webfig=yes`) |
| `default-credentials` | string or null | No | `username:password` shown in UI |
| `url-path` | string | No | URL path suffix for browser access (e.g., `/admin`) |
| `credentials` | string | No | Credential hint (alternative to default-credentials) |
| `option` | boolean | No | Whether app is optional |
| `auto-update` | boolean | No | Pull and restart containers on every boot |
| `configs` | object | No | Config file declarations with inline content |
Each key under `services:` defines one container. Required property: `image`.
| `image` | string | Container image (omit registry to use `/container/config`'s `registry-url`) |
| `container_name` | string | Explicit name; used as base for file paths under `/container` |
| `entrypoint` | string or string[] | Override default entrypoint |
| `command` | string or string[] | Override default command |
| `environment` | object or array or null | Environment variables (`KEY=value` list or `{KEY: value}
| `configs` | array of objects | Config file placements (`{source, target, mode}`) |
| `depends_on` | array or object | Service dependency ordering |
| `devices` | array of strings | Device mappings passed to container |
| `user` | string | User to run container as |
| `stop_grace_period` | string or int | Time before SIGKILL |
| `build` | object or string | Build configuration (context, dockerfile, args) |
| `healthcheck` | object | Health check (test, interval, timeout, retries, start_period) |
| `expose` | array | Internal ports (not published to host) |
| `secrets` | array of strings | Secrets to expose |
| `[accessIP]` | IP address for accessing the app from outside |
| `[accessPort]` | Primary host port for external access |
| `[containerIP]` | IP address assigned to the container |

Store files use the `.tikappstore.yaml` extension by convention.

**Note:** The `/app` endpoint requires the **container** extra package to be installed.
| `*.latest.json` | CI/strict validation | Regex patterns enforced | `^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*$` only |
| `*.editor.json` | Editor/SchemaStore UX | No regex (allows autocompletion) | Case-insensitive |

Use `.editor.json` URLs for better autocompletion at the cost of less strict validation.
- **Using `version:` key** — RouterOS ignores it; not needed
- **Uppercase env var names required** in strict validation — use `*.editor.json` for mixed case
- **Forgetting the container package** — `/app` returns 404 without the `container` extra package

content.value_statement: RouterOS /app YAML differs from docker-compose and is easy to misconfigure. This skill helps create, validate, and explain RouterOS container app definitions.
actual_capabilities: Explains RouterOS /app top-level fields, service fields, configs, volumes, and networks.
Shows supported port mapping formats for RouterOS 7.21, 7.22, and 7.23 behavior.
Provides examples for minimal apps, full apps, app store files, and placeholder usage.
Describes REST API patterns for listing apps and adding app YAML by URL.
Explains strict and editor JSON Schema variants for YAML validation.
Highlights common mistakes when converting from docker-compose to RouterOS /app YAML.
limitations: It does not install RouterOS packages or run RouterOS commands by itself.
It does not verify live router compatibility without user-provided router access.
Example credentials and images must be hardened before production use.
RouterOS beta behavior can change before stable release.

use_cases.title: Draft A New RouterOS App
use_cases.description: Create a first tikapp YAML file with services, ports, volumes, and config content.

use_cases.title: Review A Container Migration
use_cases.description: Compare a docker-compose design with RouterOS /app limits and required syntax changes.

use_cases.title: Document An App Store Entry
use_cases.description: Prepare RouterOS app store metadata and validation notes for a curated app list.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Minimal App
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a simple service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a minimal RouterOS /app YAML plan for one web container. Include ports, a short explanation, and production hardening notes.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Compose Concepts
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this docker-compose design and explain how to express the supported parts in RouterOS /app YAML. List unsupported fields separately.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Port And Placeholder Usage
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this RouterOS app design for valid port formats, placeholder usage, environment variables, and common schema mistakes.

prompt_templates.title: Design A Store Entry
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for app catalog maintainers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a RouterOS app store entry for multiple apps. Include validation strategy, schema choice, version notes, and security review points.

output_examples.input: Create a small RouterOS app for an Nginx service on host port 8080.
output_examples.output: A minimal app plan with one web service, a single port mapping, and notes about image pinning and credentials.

output_examples.input: Explain why my docker-compose file does not work as RouterOS /app YAML.
output_examples.output: A compatibility review that separates supported fields from unsupported deploy, resources, and compose-only behavior.

output_examples.input: Prepare validation guidance for tikapp files in VSCode and CI.
output_examples.output: A schema selection guide that explains strict validation, editor completion, file patterns, and expected tradeoffs.

best_practices: Pin container image versions and review updates before enabling automatic restarts.
Replace all example credentials with unique secrets before deployment.
Use strict schemas in CI and editor schemas for authoring support.
anti_patterns: Copying example passwords into a live RouterOS app.
Assuming every docker-compose field is supported by RouterOS /app.
Mixing old and new RouterOS port formats in one entry.

faq.question: Does this skill execute RouterOS commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides YAML and guidance. You decide whether to run any RouterOS command.

faq.question: Can it convert docker-compose files directly?
faq.answer: It can map supported concepts, but RouterOS /app is not fully compatible with docker-compose.

faq.question: Which RouterOS versions does it cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on RouterOS 7.21 app listing, 7.22 custom app creation, and 7.23 port format changes.

faq.question: Can it validate a file against the live schema?
faq.answer: It can explain schema choices and review structure. Live validation requires a separate validator or editor integration.

faq.question: Does it manage secrets securely?
faq.answer: It can recommend safer patterns, but users must provide and protect their own production secrets.

faq.question: Is it only for app store files?
faq.answer: No. It covers single app YAML files, store YAML arrays, schema setup, and common migration issues.
